investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The scheduler message (evidence id: failed-check.message) reports two distinct blocking conditions: (1) the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource have zero remaining capacity for that resource, and (2) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also ruled out because no lower-priority victims exist on the capacity-constrained nodes and preemption cannot help on the affinity-mismatched nodes. The result is that the agent VM was never started, no evidence was written, and the eval timed out after ~148 s, well under the 360 s outage threshold, producing a hard fail with an empty evidence object.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's nodeAffinity or nodeSelector targets only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, and those nodes are saturated. If the selector were broadened or additional nodes were labeled, scheduling might succeed.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource. If concurrent remote-agent workloads (including other eval runs or real user agents) have consumed all slots, new pods queue indefinitely. No preemption victims exist, ruling out a transient priority inversion.

Lower confidence — node-level resource leak or stuck pods: if previously scheduled remote-agent pods from earlier eval runs were not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner), their VM slots would remain consumed. The runner uses withCleanup (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1883), but a cleanup failure could leave slots occupied.

This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Preemption was also ruled out because no lower-priority victims exist on the capacity-constrained nodes and preemption cannot help on the affinity-mismatched nodes. The result is that the agent VM was never started, no evidence was written, and the eval timed out after ~148 s, well under the 360 s outage threshold, producing a hard fail with an empty evidence object.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, so each pod remained stuck for ~143–148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing the expected-output contract entirely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner never completed, no agent was provisioned, and the expected-output contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were never populated. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM node pool in production-api; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.
